source_text:
Περὶ δὲ τοῦ συνδούλου μου Βούρρου, τοῦ κατὰ θεὸν διακόνου ὑμῶν ἐν πᾶσιν εὐλογημένου, εὔχομαι παραμεῖναι αὐτὸν εἰς τιμὴν ὑμῶν καὶ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου: καὶ Κρόκος δέ, ὁ θεοῦ ἄξιος καὶ ὑμῶν, ὅν ἐξεμπλάριον τῆς ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν ἀγάπης ἀπέλαβον, κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσεν, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀναψύξαι, ἅμα Ὀνησίμῳ καὶ Βούρρῳ καὶ Εὔπλῳ καὶ Φρόντωνι, δἰ ὦν πάντας ὑμᾶς κατὰ ἀγάπην εἶδον.
ὀναίμην ὑμῶν διὰ παντός, ἐάνπερ ἄξιος ὦ. πρέπον οὗν ἐστὶν κατὰ πάντα τρόπον δοξάζειν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν δοξάσαντα ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν μιᾷ ὑποταγῇ κατηρτισμένοι, ὑποτασσόμενοι τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ, κατὰ πάντα ἦτε ἡγιασμένοι.
thought_title: Prayer for Burrhus and Crocus, and a call to unity under bishop and elders
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch writing as a prisoner on his way to martyrdom in Rome, has just praised the Ephesian church and its bishop Onesimus, and now commends two more Ephesians, Burrhus and Crocus, before urging the whole church to be united under its bishop and council of elders.
pass_a_gloss: But concerning my fellow slave Burrhus, the according to God deacon of you in all things blessed, I pray [that] he remain for honor of you and of the bishop: and Crocus too, the of God worthy and of you, whom [as] an example of the from you love I received, in all things me he refreshed, as also him the Father of Jesus Christ may refresh, together with Onesimus and Burrhus and Euplus and Fronto, through whom all of you according to love I saw. May I have joy of you through all time, if indeed worthy I am. Fitting therefore it is in every way to glorify Jesus Christ the [one] having glorified you, so that in one submission having been knit together, submitting to the bishop and to the council of elders, in all things you may be sanctified.

choices.why: Ignatius deliberately uses the language of shared slavery to Christ to express collegiality with Burrhus; 'fellow slave' keeps the force of the compound and the humility of the address.
The phrase marks Burrhus's diaconate as divinely ordered, not merely human; the literal rendering preserves the theological weight Ignatius gives to church office.

choices.english: example of the love from you
choices.why: The rare word ἐξεμπλάριον (Latin exemplarium) means a pattern or model; keeping 'example' with the source's 'from you' construction shows Crocus embodies the Ephesians' love.

choices.english: may I have joy of you
choices.why: The optative of ὀνίνημι expresses a wish for benefit or delight from someone; 'have joy of you' captures the personal, affectionate force better than a bare 'benefit from you.'
rejected: may I be blessed by you

choices.why: The perfect participle of καταρτίζω means being fitted or joined into a whole; 'knit together' conveys the organic unity Ignatius wants under one submission.
The numeral μιᾷ is emphatic: not many submissions but a single shared act of submission to bishop and elders; 'one submission' keeps that emphasis.

pass_b_english: Now about Burrhus, my fellow slave and your deacon in God's service, blessed in every way: I pray that he may remain with you for your honor and for the honor of the bishop. And Crocus, worthy of God and of you, whom I received as an example of the love that comes from you, refreshed me in every way. May the Father of Jesus Christ refresh him as well, along with Onesimus, Burrhus, Euplus, and Fronto, through whom I saw all of you in love.

May I have joy of you through all time, if only I am worthy. It is fitting, then, to glorify Jesus Christ in every way, for he has glorified you, so that you may be knit together in one submission, submitting to the bishop and the council of elders, and be sanctified in every way.
